📅 Your money: what's coming up this week and next.

1️⃣ Wednesday 18 Nov: October inflation figures from Stats SA. September was 4.5%, above the Reserve Bank's 2–4% range around its 3% target.
2️⃣ Thursday 19 Nov: the Reserve Bank's interest rate decision, around 15:00. The repo rate is 7.25% and prime is 10.75%.
3️⃣ Expected by about Sunday 22 Nov: new councils hold their first meetings and elect mayors. They will set your rates and tariffs from July 2027.
4️⃣ Coming up at month-end: official December fuel prices. Petrol is still expected to fall, but the temporary levy relief shrinks on 2 December (adding back about 50c a litre on petrol and R1.50 on diesel) and ends on 5 January.

And Black Friday is next Friday, 27 November.

Which of these matters most for your budget? 👇

text:
💰 Getting a bonus or 13th cheque this year? Here's why it can look smaller than you expected.

🔹 There's no special bonus tax. SARS treats a bonus like the rest of your pay: it's added to your income for the year and taxed at your top (marginal) rate.
🔹 Your salary has already used up the lower tax brackets, so the bonus is taxed at your top rate, and a big bonus can push part of it into a higher bracket. That's why the PAYE on it feels heavy. If your total income is below the tax threshold, you may pay no tax on it at all.
🔹 PAYE is an advance payment. If too much or too little was taken, it's squared up when you file your tax return.

Before you spend it, three questions:
1️⃣ Is there expensive debt I could pay down first, like a store card or credit card?
2️⃣ Have I set aside money for January: school fees, uniforms and the long wait to payday?
3️⃣ Can some of it go to an emergency fund?

General information, not financial advice.

text:
🏦 Thinking of a two-pot withdrawal for December? Know what it really costs first.

The rules:
🔹 You can withdraw from your savings pot once per tax year (March to February), at least R2,000.
🔹 The money is added to your income and taxed at your marginal rate. A big withdrawal can push you into a higher bracket.
🔹 If you owe SARS, it can take that tax debt from the payout first.
🔹 The tax directive and fund processing can take weeks, so the money may not arrive before Christmas. You must be registered for tax, and fees may apply.

Example (illustrative): you withdraw R20,000 and your marginal rate is 26% (roughly R237,000 to R370,000 taxable income a year). About R5,200 goes to tax, so you get about R14,800 before fees.

It's money taken from your retirement, plus the growth it would have earned. Please don't raid your retirement for Black Friday.

General information, not financial advice.

What's your plan for January costs? 👇

#MzansiMoneyMatters #TwoPot #Retirement

🤝 Stokvel payout season is close. Five ways to keep your group's money safe:

1️⃣ Write it down: a simple constitution with the rules, the contribution, the payout date and what happens if someone stops paying.
2️⃣ Use a bank account in the stokvel's name, not one member's personal account.
3️⃣ Require at least two signatories for any withdrawal.
4️⃣ Share statements with every member, every month.
5️⃣ Be careful of "investment" offers promising big, guaranteed returns before December. If it sounds too good to be true, check that the provider is registered with the FSCA first.

General information, not financial advice.

Does your stokvel have a written constitution? Send this to your stokvel's treasurer 👇
